behavioral_evidence.claim: the proposed training-only signal
behavioral_evidence.value: Directed item-to-item transitions aggregated over the training sequences (sequential co-consumption one step apart), popularity adjusted, symmetrised; plus the tree-likeness (Gromov delta) of that metric around each item.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From the training split only. For every consecutive pair (i -> j) inside a training user sequence, increment n_ij. pop_i = sum_j n_ij + sum_j n_ji. d_beh(i,j) = -log((n_ij + 1) / (sqrt(pop_i * pop_j) + 1)), exactly as in the tools-side probe. Symmetrise D_ij = (d_beh(i,j) + d_beh(j,i))/2. Set D_ij = D_max = max finite D for pairs with no observed transition in either direction, so absence is never rewarded. Neighbourhood size m = round(median_i |{j : n_ij > 0}|), clamped to [8, 50] as a documented default (not tuned). N_m(i) = the m smallest-D neighbours of i.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: The transition counts, the popularity vector, D, the neighbourhoods, the Gromov deltas and therefore the curvatures are all computed from training-split sequences only and frozen before Stage-2 step 1. Validation and test events are never read during SID construction; there is no test-time graph, no transductive propagation and no use of the Stage-3 labels. The probe itself is the training-split behaviour distance, so the coupling cannot be explained by test information entering the code.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From the Stage-2 training interaction file only: accumulate the directed count matrix n_ij over consecutive item pairs in each training user sequence and pop_i as item i's training interaction count; form d_beh; keep the K=20 smallest-d_beh neighbours per item (K is a documented default, not tuned), symmetrise the resulting sparse graph by averaging the two directions, run Prim to get the MST, precompute the path-max structure through the parent tree; sample Q=200000 quadruples of item indices uniformly to estimate the delta. All of this happens once, before the first Stage-2 step, and is written as a frozen side file.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: The count matrix, the popularity vector, the neighbour sets, the MST, the tree distances, the four-point delta, the initial curvature, the alpha scale and the lambda ratio are all functions of the training-split transition file and of nothing else; no validation or test interaction, no held-out user, and no Stage-3 feedback enters any of them. d_T is a property of the item graph, not of any evaluated user, so a test user's sequence cannot influence the SID. The probe itself is recomputed after training with the same training-split d_beh, so probe and mechanism see identical inputs and no test signal leaks into the SID construction.

behavioral_evidence.value: Sequential co-consumption and directed item transitions inside training sequences, converted into the popularity-adjusted symmetric behaviour distance d_beh(i,j) = −log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i pop_j)+1)) and then into a discrete behaviour tree whose LCA depth is the supervision target.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From the training split only. n_ij counts training sequences containing both i and j, pop_i counts training sequences containing i, and directed N(i→j) is accumulated from consecutive pairs in the same training sequence. The tree is built offline at Stage-2 initialisation by rank-64 truncated SVD of D^(−1/2) W D^(−1/2) followed by recursive bisecting 2-means (deterministic seeding, fixed iteration count) to 64 leaves at depth 6. ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set the behaviour switch to off, so D_ij is undefined, the positive set P is empty and w_ij = 0; L_geo contributes exactly zero and the run degenerates to the plain Euclidean RQ-VAE objective with the curved commitment still present but with c_i taken from the all-ones fallback (i.e. the geometry cannot express anything behavioural). Code path exists and is asserted to return a zero tensor.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full mechanism as specified: behaviour positives, behaviour weights, c_i from the measured Gromov delta, variable-curvature Poincare distance in both the contrastive and the commitment error. This is the only arm that is trained in the round.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Keep the behaviour switch on but replace the curved operator by its flat limit: d_P^{c}(a,b) -> ||a-b||, tau_ij -> 1, c_i -> 1 in the weights only (so w_ij = exp(-D_ij/Dbar_i)), and the commitment error becomes the ordinary Euclidean ||r_l - e_l||^2. This isolates how much of the gain comes from curvature rather than from the behaviour target.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only. For every consecutive pair (i -> j) inside a training user sequence, increment n_ij. pop_i = sum_j n_ij + sum_j n_ji. d_beh(i,j) = -log((n_ij + 1) / (sqrt(pop_i * pop_j) + 1)), exactly as in the tools-side probe. Symmetrise D_ij = (d_beh(i,j) + d_beh(j,i))/2. Set D_ij = D_max = max finite D for pairs with no observed transition in either direction, so absence is never rewarded. Neighbourhood size m = round(median_i |{j : n_ij > 0}|), clamped to [8, 50] as a documented default (not tuned). N_m(i) = the m smallest-D neighbours of i.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transitions aggregated over the training sequences (sequential co-consumption one step apart), popularity adjusted, symmetrised; plus the tree-likeness (Gromov delta) of that metric around each item.
ideas.cost_estimate: One-off precompute: transition counting over the training sequences, then O(24556 * m^3) quadruple evaluation with m = median positive out-degree (about 20), roughly 2e8 flops, 1-2 min on CPU, and a 24556 x m sparse table of ints/floats (~5 MB). Per step at the frozen scale (batch B = 1024, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps): one extra B x B = 1.05e6 variable-curvature distance evaluation plus its backward, about 2e7 forward flops and ~6e7 with backward, i.e. roughly +25-40% step time relative to reconstruction-only, and about +35-50 min wall clock on the whole Stage-2 run. Stage 3 is untouched (150 epochs, same protocol). No extra parameters, no extra optimiser state, no second model.
ideas.coupling_equation: L_geo = -(1/|P|) * sum_{(i,j) in P} w_ij * log[ exp(-d_P^{c_ij}(v_i, v_j)/tau_ij) / sum_{k in B} exp(-d_P^{c_ik}(v_i, v_k)/tau_ik) ], with w_ij = c_i * exp(-D_ij / Dbar_i), c_i = max(1 - 2*delta_i_norm, eps)^2, c_ij = sqrt(c_i c_j), tau_ij = 1/sqrt(c_ij), and d_P^{c}(a,b) = (1/sqrt(c)) * arcosh(1 + 2c||a-b||^2 / ((1 - c||a||^2)(1 - c||b||^2))). The behaviour term is (w_ij, P, tau) and the curved term is d_P^{c_ij}; they multiply inside one logarithm.
ideas.coupling_path: training sequences -> n_ij -> D_ij -> per-item Gromov delta delta_i -> curvature c_i -> {pair weight w_ij = c_i exp(-D_ij/Dbar_i), temperature tau_ij = 1/sqrt(c_ij), distance d_P^{c_ij}, commitment metric} -> gradient into the encoder, the RQ codebooks and the decoder -> code vectors and SIDs -> code-space distance. Removing behaviour leaves no D, no delta, no w, so the term is identically zero; removing curvature flattens d_P to the Euclidean norm, sets tau to 1 and collapses c_i, so the term becomes a plain Euclidean contrastive. Both changes alter the same sum.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If behavioural proximity is a tree-like signal, then letting each item's measured tree-likeness set its curvature will align the code space with behaviour much more strongly than any assignment-side change, because the contrastive is computed in exactly the space the probe measures and its negatives are the batch. Observable: Spearman(d_code, d_beh) rises from 0.0402 to at least 0.15 and top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap rises from 0.0124 to at least 0.08; if that holds, the SID prefixes become behaviourally predictable and Stage-3 test_recall@10 should exceed 0.065 (single run, +-0.013 noise).
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside Stage-2 training, in two places that share the same c_i: (a) the latent-side behaviour contrastive that shapes the encoder output before quantisation, and (b) the residual-quantisation commitment term at every RQ level. Nothing is applied after training and nothing is applied to a frozen SID.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball distance with variable negative curvature -c_ij, c_ij = sqrt(c_i c_j), computed on lifted points v = exp_0^{c}(u); the per-item curvature is derived from the measured Gromov delta, c_i = max(1 - 2*delta_i, eps)^2 with delta_i the normalised four-point delta of the item's behavioural neighbourhood, so c_i in (0, 1]: tree-like neighbourhoods (small delta) get unit negative curvature, Euclidean-like ones (delta near 1/2) get near-zero curvature. The same d_P is used in the RQ commitment error, so quantisation is curved too.
ideas.key_change: The encoder latent is lifted into a Poincare ball whose curvature is per item, and a behaviour contrastive over training-transition neighbours is computed with that variable-curvature distance, with temperature 1/sqrt(c_ij) and weight c_i*exp(-D_ij/Dbar_i); the same c_i-curved metric replaces the Euclidean RQ commitment error so the code assignment inherits the curvature.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition counts, the popularity vector, D, the neighbourhoods, the Gromov deltas and therefore the curvatures are all computed from training-split sequences only and frozen before Stage-2 step 1. Validation and test events are never read during SID construction; there is no test-time graph, no transductive propagation and no use of the Stage-3 labels. The probe itself is the training-split behaviour distance, so the coupling cannot be explained by test information entering the code.
ideas.motivation: The SID code space is currently organised by text reconstruction, so items that behave alike (co-transition, co-consumption) land far apart and a generative recommender cannot exploit behavioural regularity in the prefix. The probe says the same thing numerically: plain Euclidean RQ-VAE reaches only 0.0402 Spearman against the training behaviour distance and 0.0124 top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap. The fix has to be a training-objective change that makes behavioural proximity a first-class geometric target, not a codebook post-processing.
ideas.novelty: The curvature is not set by a schedule, not by prefix-transition scores and not fixed by hand: it is a measured per-item Gromov four-point delta of the behaviour metric, which says how tree-like each item's behavioural neighbourhood is. That single measured number c_i is then used four times at once (distance, temperature, pair weight, commitment error). No dead candidate uses the four-point condition, and none lets a behaviour-derived scalar set the softmax temperature. It is also not a Frechet/Karcher centroid rule, not a radial/cone assignment rule and not a metric swap on frozen code vectors: it changes the Stage-2 objective on the continuous latent that the codes are committed to.
ideas.observables: (1) Probe Spearman between code-space distance and training behaviour distance, target >= 0.15 versus the 0.0402 baseline. (2) Top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap, target >= 0.08 versus 0.0124. (3) Per-item curvature distribution: correlation between c_i and the local clustering coefficient of the behaviour graph, and the fraction of items near the c_floor. (4) Prefix behaviour predictability: for prefix lengths 1 and 2, the behaviour-weighted fraction of an item's top-10 behaviour neighbours that share its prefix, and the behaviour-weighted conditional entropy H(code_l | code_{<l}); both should drop versus baseline. (5) Codebook usage and reconstruction loss, to show the geometric term did not destroy content. (6) Stage-3 test_recall@10 with the explicit caveat that one run carries about 0.013 of noise.

risks: (1) The contrastive can overpower reconstruction, producing SIDs that cluster by behaviour but lose item identity, which the generative model then cannot discriminate; lambda balancing at initialisation only protects the start of training. (2) The transition graph is sparse and popularity-skewed, so many items have few or no observed neighbours and get a degenerate delta; the D_max clipping and the m floor are the mitigation but neighbourhood quality is not guaranteed. (3) Variable per-pair curvature is not a true metric (triangle inequality can fail), which is harmless for a softmax but makes "distance" a per-pair functional. (4) If the harness probe computes code-space distance on committed code vectors in plain Euclidean space, the gain depends on the curved commitment making codes track the latent; that link is real but weaker than the latent effect. (5) Extra ~35-50 min of Stage-2 compute may brush against the wall-clock budget.
ideas.safeguards: (1) c clipped to [1e-3, 1]; delta_i clipped to [0, 0.49] so 1-2*delta stays positive. (2) Latent norm constrained so c*||v||^2 <= 0.95^2 by construction of exp_0 (it is bounded by 1/sqrt(c)); assert max c*||v||^2 < 0.98 each step. (3) arcosh argument clamped to >= 1+1e-7; denominator clamped to >= 1e-8. (4) Pairs with no observed transition get D = D_max, never a small distance. (5) Items with fewer than 2 behaviour neighbours are excluded from P and keep the fallback c_i = 1; the count of such items is logged. (6) `if not behaviour_on: return zeros` and `if not geometry_on: use the Euclidean branch` are explicit early-exit switches, unit-tested by asserting zero output and by comparing against the flat formula. (7) Global gradient-norm clipping at 1.0 as in the baseline. (8) lambda is computed once and frozen; if L_geo(0) is non-finite the term is disabled for the run and the fact is logged (documented default, not a tuned value). (9) All probability-weighted sums over B use log_softmax with the max subtracted, so no exp overflow with tau as small as 1/sqrt(1) and distances up to ~20.
ideas.spec_equations:
# ---- one-off, before Stage-2 (training split only) ----
  for each consecutive pair (i -> j) in training sequences: n_ij += 1
  pop_i = sum_j n_ij + sum_j n_ji
  d_beh(i,j) = -log((n_ij + 1) / (sqrt(pop_i*pop_j) + 1))
  D_ij = 0.5*(d_beh(i,j) + d_beh(j,i));  D_ij = D_max if both counts are 0
  m = clip(round(median_i |{j : n_ij > 0}|), 8, 50)
  S_i = {i} union N_m(i);  scale_i = mean_{j in S_i, j != i} D_ij
  for triples (j,k,l) in S_i:
      g1 = D_ij + D_kl; g2 = D_ik + D_jl; g3 = D_il + D_jk
      delta_raw = 0.5 * max(0, g1 - max(g2, g3))
  delta_i = max(delta_raw) / (scale_i + 1e-8)          # dimensionless, ~[0, 0.5]
  delta_i = clip(delta_i, 0, 0.49)
  c_i = clip(max(1 - 2*delta_i, 1e-3)^2, 1e-3, 1.0)
  Dbar_i = mean_{j in N_m(i)} D_ij
  # ---- every Stage-2 step, batch B of 1024 items ----
  u_i = Encoder(z_i)                                    # tangent space at the origin
  v_i = tanh(sqrt(c_i)*||u_i||) / (sqrt(c_i)*||u_i|| + 1e-8) * u_i   # exp_0^{c_i}
  d_ij = (1/sqrt(c_ij)) * arcosh(1 + 2*c_ij*||v_i - v_j||^2 /
                                  ((1 - c_ij*||v_i||^2)*(1 - c_ij*||v_j||^2)))
  c_ij = sqrt(c_i*c_j); tau_ij = 1/sqrt(c_ij); w_ij = c_i*exp(-D_ij/Dbar_i)
  L_geo = mean_{i in B} ( - sum_{j in N_m(i) ∩ B} w_ij * log_softmax_k( -d_ik/tau_ik ) )
  # curved commitment, same c_i, level by level
  r_0 = u_i ; for l in 1..L:
      a = exp_0(r_{l-1}) ; b = exp_0(e_l^{code})     # both lifted into the same c_i-ball
      L_commit += d_P^{c_i}(a, b)^2
      r_l = r_{l-1} - sg(e_l^{code})                 # straight-through, as in the baseline
  L = L_recon + beta*L_commit + lambda*L_geo
  lambda = L_geo.detach() / L_recon.detach()         # evaluated once at epoch 0, step 0; frozen
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: the frozen training-transition count matrix (sparse, top-m per item), the per-item tables D_ij, Dbar_i, delta_i, c_i built once, and per step the batch of item text embeddings z_i, the current encoder weights and RQ codebooks. Outputs: a scalar L_geo, a scalar curved L_commit, the straight-through quantised latent and the codes c_i^1..c_i^L per item (hence the SIDs), plus logged per-item curvature and probe diagnostics. The operator returns gradients with respect to the encoder, all L codebooks and the decoder; it returns no new parameters.

specification.text: See SPEC EQUATIONS. In one line: L = L_recon + beta*L_commit + lambda*L_geo, where L_geo is a softmax over batch negatives of the curved distance -d_P^{c_ij}(v_i,v_j)/tau_ij and every ingredient of it (positive set, weight, temperature, curvature) is a function of the training-transition behaviour metric and of its measured Gromov delta. lambda is measured once at initialisation as L_geo(0)/L_recon(0) and frozen; there is no coupling weight to tune.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: use_behavior=False replaces the MST-sampled pairs with uniformly sampled item pairs from the same batch and replaces t_tree by the constant 0.5, leaving the curvature c_delta, the Poincare distance, beta_l, alpha and lambda identical; the term then becomes a curvature-regularised isotropic pair stress with no behavioural content, and the code exists and is checked but this arm is never trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: use_behavior=True and use_curvature=True, the single training run this round performs: behaviour-derived MST pairs and ultrametric targets under the delta-initialised trainable Poincare metric on the quantized code embedding.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: use_curvature=False replaces d_poincare_c by the Euclidean ||q_i^{:l} - q_j^{:l}|| (the c -> 0 limit of the same stress), keeping the same behaviour pairs, weights, targets, beta_l, alpha and lambda, so only the curved operation changes; the switch exists and is verified but this arm is never trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the Stage-2 training interaction file only: accumulate the directed count matrix n_ij over consecutive item pairs in each training user sequence and pop_i as item i's training interaction count; form d_beh; keep the K=20 smallest-d_beh neighbours per item (K is a documented default, not tuned), symmetrise the resulting sparse graph by averaging the two directions, run Prim to get the MST, precompute the path-max structure through the parent tree; sample Q=200000 quadruples of item indices uniformly to estimate the delta. All of this happens once, before the first Stage-2 step, and is written as a frozen side file.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-transition counts with popularity adjustment, restricted to the Stage-2 training split, turned into d_beh(i,j) = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i*pop_j)+1)) and then into an ultrametric tree distance d_T by MST path-max.
ideas.cost_estimate: Offline precompute is sub-minute CPU and about 2 MB of sparse-graph state (24556 items x 20 neighbours), no GPU. Per step at the frozen scale the extra work is roughly 2*|batch| anchors (|batch| ~ 1023 at 24556 items / 24 steps) times L=3 prefix depths, i.e. about 6000 Poincare distance evaluations in the encoder width plus one additional backward into the codebook: a low single-digit percentage increase in step time over 72000 steps (3000 epochs x 24). The encoder forward, the text encoder passes and the frozen 150-epoch Stage-3 protocol are untouched, so four-card wall clock grows by a few percent, not a factor.
ideas.coupling_equation: L_str = (1/|P|) * sum_l beta_l * sum_{(i,j) in P} w_beh(i,j) * ( d_poincare_c( exp_0^c(q_i^{:l}), exp_0^c(q_j^{:l}) ) - alpha * t_tree(i,j) )^2, with w_beh(i,j) = exp(-d_beh(i,j)/D_b) normalised over P, t_tree(i,j) = d_T(i,j)/D_T, d_poincare_c(u,v) = (2/sqrt(c)) * artanh( sqrt(c) * || (-u) (+) v || ), and c = softplus(rho) initialised from delta_tilde.
ideas.coupling_path: behaviour transitions -> d_beh -> MST ultrametric target t_ij and pair weights -> Poincare distance between prefix code embeddings under curvature c_delta -> squared stress -> gradient on codebook entries C_l, on the encoder and on rho -> next epoch's code assignment. Removing the behaviour signal removes both the target distances and the pair weights; removing the curvature reduces the same stress to a Euclidean regression on the same targets, changing the metric, the gradient scale and the ball saturation; only the coupled version uses a curvature that the behaviour graph's own tree-likeness determined.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the behaviour metric of the training graph is genuinely tree-like at the scale the SID operates on (delta_tilde well below 0.5) then a curvature set by that delta makes the ultrametric embeddable with small distortion, the curved stress makes code-space distance order items the way training transitions do, and prefix levels inherit that order because they carry most of the residual energy. It is worth keeping if the probe's Spearman rises from 0.0402 to clearly above it (order 0.09-0.15) and top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap rises from 0.0124 toward 0.03 or more, and if that transfer survives into Stage 3 as test_recall@10 above 0.065; a single run carries roughly 0.013 of seed noise, so only a margin larger than that is evidence.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside Stage-2 training, on the quantized RQ code embedding (not on the encoder's continuous latent alone), at every residual prefix depth; the curvature is a global trainable scalar shared by all depths, so the geometry acts on quantization itself, and its gradient flows back from the code assignments into the codebook.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: A Poincare ball of trainable negative curvature c = softplus(rho) + 1e-6, initialised to c_delta = 1/delta_tilde^2 from the measured four-point Gromov delta of the behaviour metric, used through the exponential map at the origin and the closed-form Poincare distance.
ideas.key_change: A single global negative curvature is initialised from the Gromov delta of the training-transition behaviour metric and then learned, and Stage-2 minimises, beside the RQ-VAE loss, a Poincare stress between quantized code embeddings of behaviour-MST-related item pairs whose target is the MST path-max distance; the gradient lands on the codebook entries and on the encoder, so both the codes and the curvature move.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The count matrix, the popularity vector, the neighbour sets, the MST, the tree distances, the four-point delta, the initial curvature, the alpha scale and the lambda ratio are all functions of the training-split transition file and of nothing else; no validation or test interaction, no held-out user, and no Stage-3 feedback enters any of them. d_T is a property of the item graph, not of any evaluated user, so a test user's sequence cannot influence the SID. The probe itself is recomputed after training with the same training-split d_beh, so probe and mechanism see identical inputs and no test signal leaks into the SID construction.
ideas.motivation: The SID code space is organised by text-embedding reconstruction, not by what users actually do, so two items that users swap for each other constantly can sit in unrelated code regions while two near-duplicate descriptions share a long prefix. The probe already shows this: the Euclidean RQ-VAE reaches only 0.0402 Spearman between code-space distance and the training-split behaviour distance, and 0.0124 top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap. The generative recommender then has to spend its prefix budget on a taxonomy that no user behaviour supports, so its beam search over prefixes drifts away from the items the user would actually take next.
ideas.novelty: Earlier rounds either changed the metric on frozen codes, or derived curvature from a prefix/transition statistic (per-level prefix-transition score, context entropy, successor profile, behaviour cone). This mechanism derives curvature from a geometric invariant of the behaviour metric itself - the sampled four-point Gromov delta - and it does not use raw graph distance as its target at all: it uses the subdominant ultrametric of the training behaviour metric (MST path-max), which is exactly the kind of metric a negatively curved space represents with low distortion. The curved distance is then applied to the quantized code embedding at every residual prefix depth, weighted by that depth's share of the residual energy, so the coarse SID levels are the ones that must first respect the behaviour tree. No relabelling, no metric swap on fixed codes: the codebook vectors themselves are displaced by a curved stress whose curvature is a measured property of the training behaviour graph.
ideas.observables: The probe Spearman between code-space distance and the training-split d_beh, expected to move from 0.0402 upward; the top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap, expected to move from 0.0124 upward; the learned curvature c and its drift from c_delta; the frozen alpha and lambda values; the per-depth weights beta_l; the prefix collision rate and the number of distinct level-1 codes as secondary cheap readouts; and finally Stage-3 test_recall@10 against 0.065 with the 0.013 single-run noise caveat stated explicitly.
risks: If delta_tilde is near 0.5 the behaviour metric is not hyperbolic at all and the measured curvature is weak, leaving the stress close to a Euclidean one; the far-pair anchors may be too weak to stop the codebook from contracting; the probe's code-space distance may be a token/prefix distance rather than a distance between code embeddings, in which case the gain arrives only indirectly through prefix alignment; and the frozen alpha and lambda, measured once, could be badly scaled for later epochs.
ideas.safeguards: artanh argument clamped at 1-1e-5 and ball radius limited by clamping the exp-map pre-image norm at atanh(0.95)/sqrt(c); curvature kept positive by softplus(rho)+1e-6; pairs with j == i dropped and pairs with t_tree = 0 skipped; weights normalised so the stress magnitude is independent of batch size; d_beh clipped to [0, log(1+N_items)] so a zero-count pair cannot produce an infinite distance; delta_tilde floored at the estimator resolution so c_delta stays finite when the graph is tree-like; alpha and lambda measured once and frozen so no epoch adapts them to the validation curve; any non-finite stress value masks that step's stress contribution and is counted in the log, and a masked fraction above one percent flags the run as numerically unreliable; the codebook is not re-initialised by the stress, so the RQ-VAE reconstruction term keeps codes separated and the far-pair targets keep the embedding from contracting. Only the both-on configuration is trained: no ablation arm, no sweep over lambda, alpha, c or the clip, and no seed repetition.
ideas.spec_equations:
Precompute: n_ij, pop_i from training transitions; d_beh(i,j) = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i*pop_j)+1)); clip d_beh to [0, log(1+N_items)].
Sparse graph: E = {(i,j) : j in topK_i d_beh(i,i')} union reversed edges; weight g_ij = mean(d_beh(i,j), d_beh(j,i)) where both directions exist, else the available one.
MST: Prim on (items, E, g) -> parent pi(i), edge weight w_e; d_T(i,j) = max_{e in path_T(i,j)} w_e; D_T = max_e w_e; t_tree = d_T/D_T in [0,1].
Delta: for q in 1..Q draw four distinct items (a,b,c,d); S1 = d_beh(a,b)+d_beh(c,d), S2 = d_beh(a,c)+d_beh(b,d), S3 = d_beh(a,d)+d_beh(b,c); delta_q = (max S - median S)/2; delta_bar = mean delta_q; D_b = mean of the six pairwise d_beh over the same quadruples; delta_tilde = clip(delta_bar/D_b, 0.05, 0.5)  (0.05 is the estimator's resolution floor, documented, not tuned).
Curvature: c_delta = 1/delta_tilde^2; rho = log(expm1(c_delta)); c = softplus(rho) + 1e-6.
Forward: z_i = f_theta(e_i); r^1 = z_i; for l=1..L: k_i^l = argmin_k ||r^l - C_l[k]||^2; r^{l+1} = r^l - C_l[k_i^l]; q_i^{:l} = sum_{m<=l} C_m[k_i^m].
Pairs: P = {(i, j_minus(i)) for i in batch} union {(i, j_plus(i)) for i in batch}, j_minus uniform over MST children of i, j_plus uniform over {j : t_tree(i,j) >= median(t_tree over P_minus)}.
Weights: w_ij = exp(-d_beh(i,j)/D_b) / mean over P of exp(-d_beh/D_b).
Ball map: v_i^{:l} = tanh(sqrt(c) * s_i) * q_i^{:l} / (sqrt(c) * s_i) for s_i = ||q_i^{:l}|| > 0, else 0, with s_i clamped to atanh(0.95)/sqrt(c).
Distance: M = (-v_i) (+) v_j = ( (1 - c||v_i||^2) v_j + (1 - c||v_j||^2) v_i ) / (1 - 2c<v_i,v_j> + c^2||v_i||^2||v_j||^2); d_c = (2/sqrt(c)) * artanh(min(sqrt(c)*||M||, 1-1e-5)).
Energy shares (measured on epoch 0, then frozen): beta_l = mean_i ||C_l[k_i^l]||^2 / sum_m mean_i ||C_m[k_i^m]||^2.
Scale (measured at end of epoch 0, then frozen): alpha = sum_P w_ij d_c(i,j) / sum_P w_ij t_tree(i,j).
Weight (measured on the first ten steps, then frozen): lambda = median_t ||grad_theta L_VAE|| / ||grad_theta L_str||.
Loss: L = L_VAE + lambda * L_str.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are the frozen per-item text embeddings e_i, the Stage-2 training transition counts (from which d_beh, the top-K neighbour sets, the MST and delta_tilde are precomputed once), the RQ-VAE encoder f_theta, codebooks C_1..C_L, and the hyperparameters already in the frozen recipe. Outputs are the L code tensors k_i^l for every training item (the SID that Stage 2 emits), the updated codebooks and encoder, the trained scalar curvature c, and a log of alpha, lambda, beta_l and the masked-step fraction; nothing else in the Stage-3 interface changes.

specification.text: Offline (CPU, once, training split only): compute n_ij directed training transitions and pop_i; form d_beh(i,j) = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i*pop_j)+1)); keep the top-K=20 neighbours of each item, symmetrise, take a minimum spanning tree T; store parent pointers and d_T(i,j) = max edge weight on the T path; sample Q=200000 item quadruples to estimate the four-point delta on d_beh, normalise it to delta_tilde and set the initial curvature c_delta = 1/delta_tilde^2. In Stage 2, each step: encode the batch, residual-quantize to get codes k_i^1..k_i^L and the code embedding q_i = sum_l C_l[k_i^l]; for each anchor i sample one near partner j_minus from i's MST children and one far partner j_plus uniformly among items whose normalised tree distance is at least the median; map each prefix embedding into the ball with the curvature-c Poincare exp map; take the Poincare distance at every prefix depth l; regress it on alpha*t_ij with behaviour weights; add lambda times that stress to the RQ-VAE loss. alpha is measured once at the end of epoch 0 and lambda once from the first ten steps' gradient-norm ratio; both are then frozen, as is the curvature's initial value.

ideas.title: Curvature measured from the behaviour graph's Gromov delta, spent as a curved stress that pulls the quantized RQ code embedding onto the behaviour graph's ultrametric tree, at every prefix depth.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: BEHAVIOUR_OFF flag in the same code: second term weight 0, so k_i^l = argmin_k d_{K_i}(x_i^l, e_{l,k}) with K_i = c0 = 1 fixed (hyperbolic quantizer, text only, no transitions). Not trained this round; switch implemented and unit-checked.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The single trained candidate: behaviour pull with w_ij, N_i and K_i from the training transition metric, and curved Poincare distances in both terms, all inside the per-level argmin. This is the only arm executed, 3000 Stage-2 epochs on four cards plus the frozen 150-epoch Stage-3 protocol.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: GEOMETRY_OFF flag: replace every d_{K_i} by Euclidean distance in both terms (delta_i and K_i still computed and logged, not used), so score = ||x_i^l - e_{l,k}||/s1 + ||e_{l,k} - g_i^l||/s2. Not trained this round; switch implemented and unit-checked.
ideas.behavior_computation: Count n_ij and pop_i over the Stage-2 training split only; d_beh(i,j) = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i*pop_j)+1)); N_i = top-4 successors by smallest d_beh; w_ij = softmax(-d_beh) over N_i; local Gromov delta delta_i from the symmetrised, shortest-path-closed transition metric on S_i; delta_ref = median delta_i. All computed once before Stage-2 training, never recomputed from validation or test interactions.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed training-split item transitions (i followed by j in a training session), with popularity adjustment.
ideas.cost_estimate: 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72000 steps. Per step the extra work is the second distance term B*K*L = 1023*256*3 ~ 786k Poincare distances (~8 MFLOP) plus two detached medians, roughly 1-3% of a baseline step (encoder/decoder over ~1023 items dominates); no extra backward graph beyond the existing straight-through path. One-off precompute is 24556 items x C(9,4)=126 quadruples (~3.1M small operations, seconds to a minute vectorised) plus one forward pass over 24556 items to fill the residual banks, ~1 epoch-equivalent = 0.03% of the 72000-step budget. Bank memory 24556*3*64*4 B ~ 18.9 MB.
ideas.coupling_equation: score_l(i,k) = d_{K_i}(x_i^l, e_{l,k})/s1 + d_{K_i}(e_{l,k}, g_i^l)/s2, where g_i^l = sum_{j in N_i} w_ij * bank[j][l] (behaviour term, w_ij = softmax_j(-d_beh(i,j))), K_i = clip(delta_ref/(delta_ref+delta_i), 0.1, 2) (behaviour-derived curvature), d_K is the Poincare distance (curved term), s1 and s2 are detached batch medians.
ideas.coupling_path: Training transitions -> n_ij, pop_i -> d_beh -> (w_ij, N_i, delta_i) -> (g_i^l, K_i) -> curved assignment score at every RQ level -> chosen code indices -> SID tuple -> frozen Stage-3 vocabulary. Removing the behaviour term zeroes g_i and fixes K_i = c0, so the argmin reverts to plain nearest code; removing the curved operator replaces d_K by Euclidean in both terms.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If transition structure is the missing organising signal, the assignment-level pull must raise the probe above the Euclidean gate, expected Spearman >= 0.10 and top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap >= 0.04 versus 0.0402 / 0.0124, because successors' residuals share codes at every level and therefore share prefixes. Stage-3 test_recall@10 should then exceed 0.065; it is reported as a single run with the explicit ~0.013 noise caveat. If the probe moves but Stage-3 does not, the generative decoder cannot exploit behaviour-organised prefixes, which is itself the informative result.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the residual quantizer's per-level assignment decision (the argmin that emits each SID digit) and in the behaviour term of that same score, during Stage-2 training only; it does not act on the codebook update rule, the decoder, or Stage-3.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball distance with item-conditioned negative curvature K_i, in closed arcosh form d_K(u,v) = (1/sqrt(K)) * arcosh(1 + 2K||u-v||^2 / ((1-K||u||^2)(1-K||v||^2))), with K_i in [0.1,2] and all points clamped to norm <= 0.7.
ideas.key_change: Each residual level assigns the code minimising a two-term curved score d_{K_i}(x_i^l, e_{l,k})/s1 + d_{K_i}(e_{l,k}, g_i^l)/s2 instead of the plain nearest-code distance, where g_i^l is the w_ij-weighted mean of the stored residuals of i's top training successors and K_i is the item curvature from the local Gromov delta of the training transition metric. The chosen indices are the SIDs; the residual recursion, reconstruction and commitment losses are unchanged.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition counts, neighbour lists, local metric and curvature are built exclusively from the Stage-2 training split before the run starts; validation and test sessions are never read by the SID builder, the banks are filled only from training items, and Stage-3 consumes the frozen SIDs with no interaction feature at inference. No per-epoch statistics from held-out data enter the SID construction.
ideas.motivation: Text-only RQ-VAE SIDs cluster by surface semantics, so items that users actually transition between receive unrelated code prefixes (probe Spearman 0.0402, top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap 0.0124). The recommender therefore has to learn transition structure from SID tokens that were never organised for it. Previous fixes changed the codebook update, a per-level scalar, a radius or a post-hoc score; none changed which code wins at quantization time. This idea changes the assignment decision itself, using the training transition graph and a curved metric, so behaviourally related items are forced into nearby codes during Stage-2.
ideas.novelty: (1) the curvature of the quantization metric is an ITEM-level quantity derived from the local Gromov delta of the training transition metric, not a global constant, a per-level value, or an entropy-derived radius; (2) the behaviour signal enters the per-level argmin as a second geodesic term pointing at the curvature-matched centroid of the item's successors' stored residuals, not as a codebook update, a relabelling, or a suffix on an unchanged quantizer; (3) the two distance terms are unit-scaled by detached batch medians, so the coupling weight is derived (=1) and no sweep is needed. No successor-weighted Frechet update, no prefix cone, no successor-profile smoothing, no radial re-ranking, no metric swap on frozen code vectors.
ideas.observables: Probe after Stage-2 exactly as in the tools-side probe (Spearman between code-space distance and d_beh, top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap) with before numbers 0.0402 / 0.0124 and after numbers recorded; per-level code usage entropy and the K_i distribution (collapse check); prefix behaviour predictability as conditional entropy H(k_l | k_<l) over training items and held-out teacher-forced prefix accuracy; Stage-3 test_recall@10 with the single-run ~0.013 caveat.
risks: The successor pull can concentrate level-1 codes and starve the codebook (monitor per-level usage entropy; the equally unit-scaled text term is the only counterweight). Local delta estimates are noisy for low-degree or disconnected items (fallback delta_ref). Per-item curvature makes the distance a family of Poincare metrics rather than one global manifold. Behaviour smoothing may overwrite fine text distinctions needed for cold or long-tail items, and Stage-3 may lose the SID diversity beam search needs. One run cannot separate these effects from seed noise.
ideas.safeguards: Clamp every ball coordinate to norm 0.7 = 0.999/sqrt(K_max) with K_max = 2 so 1-K||u||^2 >= 1e-3; clamp the arcosh argument to >= 1+1e-7 with a stable arcosh; clamp K_i to [0.1,2]; floor s1, s2 and delta_ref at 1e-6; detach s1, s2, w_ij, delta_i, K_i and the bank so the behaviour target never back-propagates through the precompute; empty N_i or disconnected S_i gives g_i^l = x_i^l (stop-grad) and delta_i = delta_ref; replace non-finite distances by the batch maximum finite distance before the argmin; keep the baseline codebook-usage reset and beta unchanged; assert that no validation or test item id appears in the startup transition table.
ideas.spec_equations: d_K(u,v) = (1/sqrt(K)) * arcosh(1 + 2*K*||u-v||^2 / ((1-K*||u||^2)*(1-K*||v||^2))). d_beh(i,j) = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i*pop_j)+1)); l_ij = (d_beh(i,j)+d_beh(j,i))/2; D = shortest_path(l) on S_i. delta_i = max_{a,b,c,p in S_i} 0.5*(max(S1,S2,S3) - mid(S1,S2,S3)), S1 = D(a,b)+D(c,p), S2 = D(a,c)+D(b,p), S3 = D(a,p)+D(b,c). delta_ref = median_i delta_i; K_i = clip(delta_ref/(delta_ref+delta_i), 0.1, 2). w_ij = exp(-d_beh(i,j)) / sum_{j' in N_i} exp(-d_beh(i,j')); g_i^l = sum_j w_ij * bank[j][l]. score_l(i,k) = d_{K_i}(x_i^l,e_{l,k})/s1 + d_{K_i}(e_{l,k},g_i^l)/s2; k_i^l = argmin_k score_l(i,k). e_{l,k} = exp_0(v_{l,k}) = tanh(||v_{l,k}||/2) * v_{l,k}/||v_{l,k}|| (reference curvature 1); log_0(x) = 2*artanh(||x||) * x/||x||. u_i^1 = Enc(text_i); x_i^l = clamp(exp_0(u_i^l), 0.7); u_i^{l+1} = log_0(x_i^l) - v_{l,k_i^l}. L = ||Dec(sum_l v_{l,k_i^l}) - text_i||^2 + beta * sum_l ||sg(log_0(x_i^l)) - v_{l,k_i^l}||^2, beta the baseline value unchanged. Straight-through: hard index, the gradient to the encoder passes through the identity path as in the baseline.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: item text embeddings (24556 x d), training-split transition counts, baseline codebook size K and levels L, baseline encoder/decoder. Outputs: a K^L SID vocabulary, one SID tuple per item, the per-item K_i array, per-level code usage counts, the two probe numbers, and the Stage-3 recall. Internal operator: given residuals x_i^l (ball coordinates), code points e_{l,k}, bank rows and (w_ij, K_i, s1, s2), it returns the hard code indices for all levels and the refreshed residual bank.

specification.text: Precompute once, before Stage-2, from training-split sessions only: n_ij = directed transition counts, pop_i = sum_j n_ij + sum_j n_ji, d_beh(i,j) = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i*pop_j)+1)); N_i = 4 successors with n_ij>0 and smallest d_beh; w_ij = softmax_j(-d_beh(i,j)) over N_i. Symmetrise l_ij = (d_beh(i,j)+d_beh(j,i))/2; S_i = {i} union N_i union 4 predecessors with largest n_ji (|S_i| <= 9). On the induced subgraph of S_i take shortest-path closure of l (a genuine metric); if disconnected set delta_i = delta_ref. delta_i = max over quadruples (a,b,c,p) in S_i of (largest - second largest)/2 of the three sums d(a,b)+d(c,p), d(a,c)+d(b,p), d(a,p)+d(b,c). delta_ref = median_i delta_i; K_i = clip(delta_ref/(delta_ref+delta_i), 0.1, 2); c0 = 1 is the documented unit-curvature default. During Stage-2, for batch B and level l = 1..L: u_i^1 = Enc(text_i); x_i^l = exp_0(u_i^l) (reference curvature 1), clamp ||x|| <= 0.7; g_i^l = sum_{j in N_i} w_ij * bank[j][l] (stop-grad); s1 = median_i min_k d_{K_i}(x_i^l,e_{l,k}), s2 = median_i min_k d_{K_i}(e_{l,k},g_i^l), both detached and floored at 1e-6; k_i^l = argmin_k [d_{K_i}(x_i^l,e_{l,k})/s1 + d_{K_i}(e_{l,k},g_i^l)/s2]; e_{l,k} = exp_0(v_{l,k}); u_i^{l+1} = log_0(x_i^l) - v_{l,k_i^l}; bank[i][l] <- detach(x_i^l); L = ||Dec(sum_l v_{l,k_i^l}) - text_i||^2 + beta * sum_l ||sg(log_0(x_i^l)) - v_{l,k_i^l}||^2, exactly the baseline losses.

ideas.title: Behaviour-local Gromov-delta curvature steering a successor-residual pull inside the RQ-VAE code assignment

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: BEHAVIOUR_ON = False drops the transition pairs and zeroes the behaviour term, leaving the Möbius quantiser, geodesic assignment and curved SID point trained only by text reconstruction. The code is present and correct but this arm is not trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: BEHAVIOUR_ON = True and GEOMETRY_ON = True, the curved Möbius quantiser plus the behaviour-tree Gromov target, is the single configuration trained in the formal run on the frozen 3000-epoch four-card Stage-2 budget and the frozen 150-epoch Stage-3 protocol.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: GEOMETRY_ON = False replaces Möbius addition with vector addition, the Möbius residual with the ordinary residual, geodesic distance with Euclidean distance, and the ball Gromov product with its Euclidean identity (x·y)_o = 0.5(|x|² + |y|² − |x−y|²), while the same frozen tree and LCA-depth targets stay on. Not trained this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only. n_ij counts training sequences containing both i and j, pop_i counts training sequences containing i, and directed N(i→j) is accumulated from consecutive pairs in the same training sequence. The affinity is W_ij = exp(−d_beh(i,j)) restricted to each item's top-50 neighbours and symmetrised as (W + Wᵀ)/2. The tree is built offline at Stage-2 initialisation by rank-64 truncated SVD of D^(−1/2) W D^(−1/2) followed by recursive bisecting 2-means (deterministic seeding, fixed iteration count) to 64 leaves at depth 6. Each item receives a frozen 6-bit leaf code, and each training transition (i,j) is stored with (leaf(i), leaf(j)).
ideas.behavior_signal: Sequential co-consumption and directed item transitions inside training sequences, converted into the popularity-adjusted symmetric behaviour distance d_beh(i,j) = −log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i pop_j)+1)) and then into a discrete behaviour tree whose LCA depth is the supervision target.
ideas.cost_estimate: Offline once, before the 3000 epochs: sparse top-50 kNN over 24556 items, a rank-64 randomised SVD of a ~1e6-nnz affinity, six bisecting levels, roughly 3 to 8 minutes on one card, not repeated. Per step at the frozen scale (batch about 1024 of the 24556 training items, 24 steps per epoch, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps): assignments cost L*K*d = 3*256*32 about 25k dot products per sample, about 25 MFLOP per step; three Möbius sums are negligible; the Gromov term evaluates 2*1024 pair distances of dimension 32. Overhead is about 2 to 4 percent of the baseline step, extra memory is one L*K*d atom table, and there is no extra epoch, card or dataloader pass.
ideas.coupling_equation: L_hier = mean_i [ ( ((x_i·x_j)_o − (x_i·x_j')_o) / G_max ) − ( g_T(i,j) − g_T(i,j') ) ]² with x_i = a_{1,k1} ⊕ … ⊕ a_{L,kL} (curved term) and g_T(i,j) = depth(LCA(leaf(i), leaf(j))) / 6 (behaviour term), where j is a stored training successor of i and j' is a uniformly sampled item.
ideas.coupling_path: Training transitions give n_ij, pop_i and d_beh, which give the affinity, which gives the frozen tree and the LCA-depth target g_T. In parallel, z is mapped to the ball, quantised by Möbius residuals into atoms and summed by Möbius addition into x_i. Both meet in a single term: removing the behaviour tree zeroes g_T and the loss loses all behaviour content, while removing the curvature replaces the Möbius sum and the Gromov product with a vector sum and Euclidean distance, so each switch changes the gradient that reaches the atoms and the encoder at every step.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If LCA depth captures the co-consumption hierarchy and the curved code space realises that tree with low distortion, matching Gromov products pulls true successors closer than the Euclidean baseline, visible first as top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap well above 0.0124 (target 0.025 or more) and Spearman well above 0.0402 (target 0.07 or more), then as Stage-3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 under the standing caveat of about 0.013 single-run noise.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Curvature acts inside Stage-2 training at four connected places: the encoder-to-ball map, the residual quantiser (Möbius subtraction plus geodesic nearest-atom selection at every level), the SID point formed as a Möbius sum of the selected atoms, and the Gromov product used in the behaviour loss; the atom table is also ball-parametrised, so every atom gradient is a curved-space gradient.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincaré ball of fixed negative curvature c = 1 with working radius R = 1 − 1e−3, Möbius addition u ⊕ v = ((1 + 2⟨u,v⟩ + |v|²) u + (1 − |u|²) v) / (1 + 2⟨u,v⟩ + |u|²|v|²), geodesic distance d(u,v) = 2 artanh(|(−u) ⊕ v|), and the origin-anchored Gromov product (x·y)_o = 0.5 ( d(x,o) + d(y,o) − d(x,y) ), normalised by G_max = 2 artanh(R).
ideas.key_change: The RQ residual and the SID point become Möbius operations inside a Poincaré ball (r_l = (−a_l) ⊕ r_{l−1}, x_i = a_1 ⊕ … ⊕ a_L) and every codebook atom is a trainable ball point selected by geodesic distance, so the quantiser is genuinely curved. One extra loss term forces the curved Gromov products of the SID points to reproduce the LCA-depth Gromov products of the behaviour tree, so the same pathway that assigns codes also carries the behaviour gradient into the atoms and the encoder.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Every count, affinity, embedding, leaf code and transition pair is computed exclusively from training-split sequences; validation and test interactions are never read; no Stage-3 signal enters the tree; the tree is frozen before the first Stage-2 epoch, so no validation-driven selection can act on it; and the mechanism needs no early stopping or model selection, so no evaluation split is consulted at any point.
ideas.motivation: The frozen semantic-ID pipeline has to place behaviourally adjacent items near each other in code space, yet the plain Euclidean RQ-VAE reaches only Spearman 0.0402 and top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap 0.0124 against the training-split popularity-adjusted transition distance d_beh. The failure is structural: a Euclidean product quantiser cannot represent a tree-like, negatively curved behaviour metric, so co-consumed items fall into unrelated cells even when their text embeddings agree. A behaviour-induced tree, by contrast, embeds in hyperbolic space with arbitrarily low distortion, so the quantiser is given a curved arithmetic and the tree becomes the target the curvature has to realise.
ideas.novelty: The earlier rounds moved per-level curvature from prefix entropy (CURVCTRL-SID), ranked items radially by context entropy (BRad-RQ), made codebook updates successor-weighted Fréchet means (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook), and split curvature across branching experts (BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ). None of them constructs a behaviour tree, none uses the Gromov product, and none writes the two sides of the objective as the same geometric quantity. This proposal adds two new objects: a spectral bisecting-k-means tree over the popularity-adjusted transition affinity, and an LCA-depth Gromov-product target matched against the Gromov products of Möbius-summed SID points, with the curved residual and geodesic assignment living inside the quantiser rather than being a post-hoc metric or a relabelling of fixed codes.
ideas.observables: Before Stage 3, the tools-side probe is re-run exactly as specified with d_beh over training transitions only: code-space Spearman against d_beh and top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap, compared with 0.0402 and 0.0124, and the proposal is a candidate only if both improve. During training, mean atom radius, the fraction of atoms within 0.9 R, per-level code usage, reconstruction MSE and the behaviour-term value are logged. After Stage 3, test_recall@10 is reported with the explicit caveat that a single run carries about 0.013 of noise; no early stopping, sweep or seed repetition supports the claim.
risks: A six-level tree makes the target nearly binary, so the ordering signal may be too coarse; the behaviour gradient may fight text reconstruction and damage the decoder, showing as worse Stage-3 recall even with a better probe; ball saturation could push atoms to the boundary and make geodesic distances uninformative; the tools-side probe may compute code-space distance as Euclidean on stored parameters rather than as a geodesic, so the Euclidean-on-coordinates variant is reported alongside; sparse transitions make n_ij noisy for tail items and can inflate leaf assignment.
ideas.safeguards: Add 1e−8 to every Möbius denominator, which for c = 1 is bounded below by (1−|u|²)(1−|v|²); clamp the artanh argument to 1 − 1e−6 and radii to R = 1 − 1e−3; keep atoms inside the ball by construction through the smooth R·tanh(θ)/sqrt(1+|tanh(θ)|²) map; use the relative difference-of-pairs form of L_hier so a global contraction of all SID points cannot reduce the loss, which removes the collapse failure mode without a tunable margin; keep reconstruction on unit-normalised text embeddings so beta = 1 is dimensionless rather than tuned; freeze the tree before training so leaf codes cannot co-adapt; skip items with no training successor rather than substituting a random positive; clip gradients only with the existing frozen Stage-2 recipe, adding no new constant.
ideas.spec_equations: [1] t = tanh(z); p = R·t / sqrt(1 + |t|²); a = R·tanh(θ) / sqrt(1 + |tanh(θ)|²). [2] Möbius u ⊕ v as defined above; inverse −u = −u; d(u,v) = 2 artanh(|(−u) ⊕ v|). [3] r_0 = p; k_l = argmin_k d(r_{l−1}, a_{l,k}); r_l = (−a_{l,k_l}) ⊕ r_{l−1}; q = concat_l(flatten(a_{l,k_l})); L_recon = |Dec(q) − e_text|². [4] x_i = a_{1,k1(i)} ⊕ … ⊕ a_{L,kL(i)}. [5] (x·y)_o = 0.5(d(x,o) + d(y,o) − d(x,y)), d(x,o) = 2 artanh(|x|), G_max = 2 artanh(R). [6] offline: W_ij = exp(−d_beh(i,j)) on top-50 neighbours, symmetrised, rank-64 SVD of D^(−1/2) W D^(−1/2), bisecting 2-means to 64 leaves, g_T(i,j) = common_prefix_len(leaf(i), leaf(j)) / 6. [7] L_hier as in the coupling equation; L = L_recon + 1.0·L_hier. [8] Straight-through: the forward code comes from the argmin, the encoder gradient passes as identity through the selection, and atom gradients are taken directly and through the Möbius sums in x_i.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are a training batch of item ids with their text embeddings, the encoder outputs z, the atom table θ of shape L × K × d, the frozen 6-bit leaf codes, and for each batch item one stored training successor j and one uniform negative j'. Outputs are the L selected code indices per item (the SIDs), the SID ball points x_i, the scalars L_recon and L_hier, and gradients with respect to the atom table, the encoder and the decoder.

specification.text: Fix curvature c = 1 and working radius R = 1 − 1e−3. The encoder output z is mapped into the ball, atoms are parametrised inside it, RQ runs by Möbius subtraction, assignment is by geodesic distance, and L = L_recon + L_hier, where L_hier is a relative (ranking) Gromov-product match to a frozen behaviour tree. The tree is built once before Stage 2 from the training-split popularity-adjusted transition affinity: top-50 sparse kNN, rank-64 normalised-spectrum embedding, recursive bisecting 2-means to 64 leaves at depth 6. Every constant is structural or numerical (R from the ball boundary, 64 leaves as a documented default of about 384 items per leaf, beta = 1 because both losses are dimensionless, c = 1) and none is swept.

ideas.title: Behaviour-tree Gromov products matched by a Möbius-summed curved RQ-VAE code space

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: A switch `use_behaviour` set to False; d_beh is replaced by a constant matrix, the batch is uniformly sampled, L_GW reduces to a variance penalty on D_P and the run is the plain Euclidean/curved RQ-VAE. Implemented and correct, not trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: `use_behaviour=True` and `curvature_mode="poincare"` with kappa = -1/delta^2 from the measured delta; this is the single trained arm.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: A switch `curvature_mode="euclidean"`; kappa is set to 0, D_P becomes ||z_i - z_j||, everything else including the behaviour target and the batches is unchanged. Implemented and correct, not trained in this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only, count directed transitions n_ij, item popularity pop_i (training interactions), form the sparse matrix d_beh(i,j) = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i*pop_j)+1)), symmetrise by elementwise min, keep the top-32 neighbours per item, and materialise the 2-hop fallback for pairs inside a sampled batch.
ideas.behavior_signal: Popularity-adjusted, symmetrised directed item-transition distance over training-split transitions, used both as the alignment target and as the kNN that constructs each batch.
ideas.cost_estimate: One-off CPU precompute of the sparse behaviour kNN and the delta estimate (a few minutes, outside the 3000-epoch budget). Per step only ~9-10k pairs are evaluated, so the extra cost is vectorised Poincare distance plus a sparse lookup: roughly +3-5% wall clock, about +0.3 to +0.6 h over 72k steps (3000 epochs x 24 steps) on four cards. No extra parameters, no extra forward pass.
ideas.coupling_equation: L_GW = mean_{(i,j) in P} [ D_P(z_i, z_j ; kappa = -1/delta^2) / med(D_P)  -  d_beh(i,j) / med(d_beh) ]^2, with the neighbour set P drawn from the behaviour kNN and delta measured on the behaviour tree.
ideas.coupling_path: d_beh -> tree T -> delta -> kappa -> Poincare distance D_P(kappa) -> normalised GW discrepancy against d_beh -> gradient into encoder and codebooks -> SID assignment. Removing the behaviour signal removes the target and the neighbour-anchored batches, so L_GW vanishes and Stage 2 is the plain RQ-VAE. Removing the curvature sends kappa to 0, D_P to the Euclidean distance, and changes every gradient in the term.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If behaviour adjacency is close to tree-like (small delta), a single constant-curvature embedding can realise it with low distortion, and forcing code distances to match it puts transition information into the SID prefixes. Observable as probe Spearman rising above 0.0402 and top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap above 0.0124, with a matching rise in Stage-3 test_recall@10 above 0.065; a single run, so ~0.013 of recall noise is part of the reading.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the Stage-2 training objective, on the pairwise distance matrix between decoded code vectors; it therefore shapes the encoder and the RQ codebooks, not a post-hoc metric.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball distance with fixed negative curvature kappa = -1/delta^2, delta measured from the behaviour tree and clipped relative to the tree diameter; no trainable curvature.
ideas.key_change: Stage-2 loss gains one term, L_GW, the discrepancy between normalised pairwise Poincare distances among the batch's decoded code vectors and normalised pairwise behaviour distances among the same items; gradients flow through the straight-through quantizer into both the encoder and the codebooks. The Poincare curvature is a single frozen constant kappa = -1/delta^2, where delta is the estimated 4-point hyperbolicity of a tree built on training transitions.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition counts, popularity, kNN table, the tree T and delta are all computed before Stage-2 starts from the training split only. Validation and test interactions are never read by the SID construction, the batch sampler, the curvature estimate or the loss; the probe itself is computed after training and never feeds back.
ideas.motivation: RQ-VAE Semantic IDs are trained to reconstruct item content, so code-space neighbourhoods reflect content similarity rather than co-consumption. Two items that users actually move between land far apart in code space, and the stage-3 generator has to memorise the transition instead of reading it off the SID prefix. The frozen probe exposes exactly this (Spearman 0.0402, top-10 overlap 0.0124 for the plain Euclidean RQ-VAE).
ideas.novelty: The previous mechanisms act per item or per level: behaviour-ranked radial assignment (BRad-RQ), per-level curvature scheduled by a hard prefix-transition score (CURVCTRL-SID), Frechet successor-weighted codebook updates. This one never touches the assignment weights, the codebook update rule or the per-level curvature schedule. It adds a single batch-level term that aligns the entire pairwise distance structure of the code space to the behaviour distance, and it *measures* how hyperbolic the behaviour graph actually is, then fixes the curvature from that measurement instead of scheduling or tuning it.
ideas.observables: Probe Spearman between code-space distance and training behaviour distance (baseline 0.0402); top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap (baseline 0.0124); per-level prefix behaviour predictability (accuracy of predicting the true next item's level-l code from the context prefix, l = 1..4); codebook usage entropy; Stage-3 test_recall@10 against the 0.065 target.
risks: The behaviour graph may be far from tree-like, giving a small |kappa| and an almost Euclidean term; the median normalisation can be dominated by the uniform random items and flatten the gradient; sampled neighbour pairs may be too few per batch to move the codebook; the probe may improve while Stage 3 does not, because matching distances is not the same as making prefixes predictive.
ideas.safeguards: Clamp the Poincare radius to 1-1e-5 before artanh; add 1e-8 inside artanh and inside the log; clip delta to a diameter-relative interval so kappa stays finite and bounded; guard medians with 1e-6; drop pairs with no observed or 2-hop behaviour path instead of imputing a large distance; skip L_GW for a step if fewer than 512 valid pairs remain; keep the straight-through gradient magnitude clipped to the RQ-VAE's existing gradient clip.
ideas.spec_equations:
d_beh(i,j) = -log((n_ij + 1) / (sqrt(pop_i * pop_j) + 1));  d_beh <- min(d_beh, d_beh^T)
  T = single_linkage(d_beh);  delta = max_Q [ (s1 + s2 - s3)/2 ] over sampled quadruples Q, s1>=s2>=s3 the three pairwise tree sums
  delta <- clip(delta, 0.01*diam(T), diam(T));  kappa = -1/delta^2
  z_i = decode(sid_i) via straight-through;  u_i = exp_0(z_i), ||u_i|| <- min(||u_i||, 1-1e-5)
  D_P(i,j) = (2/sqrt|kappa|) * atanh( sqrt|kappa| * || (-u_i) xor u_j || )
  Dhat_P = D_P / median(D_P);  dhat = d_beh / median(d_beh)
  L = L_RQVAE + mean_{(i,j) in P} (Dhat_P(i,j) - dhat(i,j))^2
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: training transition counts n_ij, training popularity pop_i, the batch's decoded code vectors z_i (B x d), the precomputed sparse d_beh table, the scalar delta and kappa. Outputs: a scalar L_GW and its gradient with respect to z_i (hence to the encoder weights and codebook entries); the batch sampler also returns the neighbour-anchored index set.

specification.text: (1) Build the training-only behaviour distance d_beh(i,j) = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i*pop_j)+1)), symmetrised as min(d_beh(i,j), d_beh(j,i)), from training-split directed transitions only. (2) Build a single-linkage (or neighbour-joining) tree T over the 24556 items from d_beh, estimate delta by sampling 2000 deterministic quadruples and taking max over quadruples of (largest two of the three pairwise sums minus the third)/2; clip delta to [0.01*diam(T), diam(T)]; set kappa = -1/delta^2. (3) At each step, form a batch of 128 anchors, each with its 8 strongest training behaviour neighbours, plus 128 uniform random items: B = 1152. (4) Decode code vectors z_i from the straight-through SID embedding, map to the Poincare ball with exp_0 and clamp radius to 1-1e-5. (5) Compute D_P(i,j) = (2/sqrt|kappa|) artanh(sqrt|kappa| * ||(-z_i) xor z_j||) for pairs present in the batch; compute d_beh for the same pairs from the sparse precomputed table (pairs without an observed transition fall back to their 2-hop shortest path in the transition graph, and are dropped if still absent). (6) Normalise both matrices by their batch medians; L_GW = mean over pairs of (Dhat_P - dhat_beh)^2. Total loss = L_RQVAE + 1.0 * L_GW.

ideas.title: Gromov-delta-calibrated Poincare distance-matrix alignment of the RQ-VAE code space to the training behaviour graph.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: a_i := 0 for every item, so t_i = x_i and the anchors are never used; the curved residual quantizer, the trainable K and all other code paths are unchanged. This run must reproduce the geometry-only behaviour, and the code exists but is not trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full LCB-RQ as specified, trained once for 3000 Stage-2 epochs on four cards with the frozen Stage-3 protocol of 150 epochs, no early stopping, no sweep, no second seed.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: K -> 0, i.e. arcosh replaced by the Euclidean limit, exp/log replaced by identity, Frechet mean replaced by the arithmetic mean of neighbour embeddings and the residual chain replaced by z - sum q, while pi_ij, m_i and a_i stay active; this is a behaviour-smoothed plain Euclidean RQ-VAE.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only, scan every user session; for every pair of item positions (p, q) with 0 < |p - q| <= 5 in the same session add 1 to c_ij. Set pop_i = sum_j c_ij, define w_ij = c_ij / ( sqrt(pop_i * pop_j) + 1 ), keep the top 20 neighbours per item by w_ij, symmetrise by max, row-normalise to pi_ij, and store the sparse list once before Stage-2. The 5 and the 20 are documented defaults of the graph construction, not tuned constants of the loss.
ideas.behavior_signal: Symmetric, windowed session co-consumption with popularity adjustment, i.e. an undirected version of the transition signal rather than the directed successor counts used by the earlier rounds.
ideas.cost_estimate: Anchor construction is a one-off pass over 24556 items x at most 20 neighbours x 3 fixed-point iterations of exp/log, roughly 1.5M exp/log evaluations, seconds on one GPU, done once before epoch 1 and frozen. Per training step the extra work is B x L exp/log pairs for the curved residual chain (B = batch, L = 3 levels, about 1.5k-6k exp/log per step) plus one Lorentz distance matrix B x K per level. At the frozen scale (24 steps/epoch x 3000 epochs = 72000 steps) this is about 1.1e8-4.3e8 extra exp/log evaluations in total, roughly 3-6 percent wall-clock over the baseline Stage-2 and zero extra epochs; Stage-3, the decoder forward pass and the sequence model are untouched.
ideas.coupling_equation: t_i = exp^K_{x_i}( a_i * log^K_{x_i}( b_i ) ), with b_i = argmin_b sum_j pi_ij * d_K(b, x_j)^2 and a_i = m_i / (m_i + m_ref), m_ref = median_i(m_i), m_i = sum_j w_ij; the level-l quantizer then minimizes d_K(p_l, c_l) with p_l obtained from the transported residual r_l, so the same K appears in the behaviour pull and in the code geometry.
ideas.coupling_path: Training split -> co-consumption graph -> row-normalised pi_ij and mass m_i -> Lorentz Frechet anchor b_i -> geodesic blend t_i = exp_{x_i}(a_i log_{x_i}(b_i)) -> curved residual quantization of t_i -> code assignment and codebook update -> SID -> Stage-3. Behaviour sets the direction and the magnitude of the pull; curvature sets the geodesic along which the pull happens and the shape of every residual after level 1. Setting the behaviour term to zero gives t_i = x_i and the curved RQ still runs; setting K to 0 (Euclidean limit) removes the geodesic blend and the curved residuals and leaves a plain behaviour-smoothed Euclidean RQ-VAE. Both switches therefore change the same tensor that the quantizer consumes.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If behaviour-coherent quantization targets are what the SID is missing, then co-consumed items must land in the same or adjacent codes, so the two probe numbers should both rise well above 0.0402 and 0.0124 (target at least 0.10 / 0.05) and the learned curvature should stay bounded away from 0, which is observable as a non-degenerate K and as a shrinking mean geodesic pull distance ||log^K_{x_i}(t_i)|| over epochs; only then is a Stage-3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 plausible, and that number is reported with the explicit single-run caveat of about 0.013 noise.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Three places in Stage-2, all tied to the same K: (i) construction of the per-item quantization target (geodesic blend and Frechet anchor), (ii) the RQ assignment and commitment term, which use d_K instead of squared Euclidean distance, (iii) the residual chain, where level l+1 quantizes p_l = exp^K_o of the transported residual instead of the vector difference z - sum q.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: The Lorentz hyperboloid L^D_K with trainable positive curvature K = softplus(theta) + 1e-3, initialized so that K = 1; Minkowski inner product <x,y>_L = -x_0 y_0 + x.y; d_K(x,y) = (1/sqrt(K)) * arcosh(-K <x,y>_L); exp^K_o and log^K_o at the origin o = (1/sqrt(K), 0, ..., 0); Lorentz Frechet mean by three tangent-space fixed-point iterations; and geodesic residual quantization, in which each RQ level encodes a tangent vector at the previously chosen code.
ideas.key_change: Precompute, once from the training split, a symmetric popularity-adjusted co-consumption graph and a per-item Lorentz barycentre of neighbours' text points; during Stage-2 replace each item's quantization point by the geodesic blend of its own text point and that anchor, with the blend weight fixed by measured co-consumption mass, and replace the Euclidean residual recursion by Lorentz exp/log residual quantization with a trainable curvature.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The co-consumption counts are read only from the training split sequences; validation and test interactions are never touched, and the resulting anchor table is computed once before epoch 1 and frozen, so no validation or test signal can enter the SID construction. The probe and Stage-3 read the frozen SIDs afterwards and never feed back.
ideas.motivation: Behaviourally co-consumed items (same session, close positions) currently get unrelated SIDs because Stage-2 only reconstructs an item's own text embedding; nothing in the objective asks two items that co-occur to share a prefix. The probe numbers of the plain Euclidean RQ-VAE (Spearman 0.0402, top-10 overlap 0.0124) show the code space is behaviour-blind. This proposal moves the quantization target itself along a geodesic toward a behaviour anchor, so co-consumed items are quantized from nearly the same point and must share codes.
ideas.novelty: Earlier mechanisms here acted on the codebook update (successor-weighted Frechet means), on per-level curvature from prefix-transition scores, on radial position from context entropy, on cones, on mixed-curvature fibres and on recursive graph cuts. None of them moves the item-side quantization target. LCB-RQ changes what is fed to the quantizer: each item's Lorentzian target is a geodesic barycentre between its own text point and the Lorentz Frechet mean of its co-consumed neighbours' text points, and the whole residual chain then runs in the curved space, so curvature re-shapes level-2 and level-3 residuals rather than only a distance.
ideas.observables: The exact probe of this round: Spearman between code-space distance and d_beh = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i pop_j)+1)), and top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap, both before (0.0402 / 0.0124) and after; the learned K; the mean geodesic pull ||log^K_{x_i}(t_i)|| per epoch; code-usage entropy and prefix counts (recorded, not gating); and Stage-3 test_recall@10 with the roughly 0.013 single-run caveat.
risks: Over-pulling collapses many items onto one prefix, which raises raw overlap but flattens the code-distance distribution and can lower Spearman and destroy reconstruction, so the weight must be mass-derived and the target clamped inside a radius shell. Curvature may drift to 0, making the geometry arm identical to the Euclidean one; the softplus parameterisation plus an initialization at K = 1 and a lower clamp at 1e-3 guards this but does not prove it. Items with no co-consumption get a_i = 0 and behave exactly like the baseline, so a sparse training split would make the whole mechanism a no-op on most items. Reconstruction of the original text embedding is no longer directly optimised for pulled items, which can hurt Stage-3 if the generator relies on literal text content; a possible symptom is a good probe and a flat or worse recall.
ideas.safeguards: clamp the arcosh argument to at least 1 + 1e-7 and at most 1e12; enforce the hyperboloid constraint by re-projecting every point with x <- x / sqrt(-K <x,x>_L) after each update; clamp tangent norms to R_max = 1.05 * R to stop boundary blow-up; clamp K into [1e-3, 10] with softplus so the Euclidean limit is reachable but never reached; use float64 for the anchor precompute and float32 for training; if an item has m_i = 0 set a_i = 0 and skip it in the anchor loop; guard the transport with a norm floor of 1e-8; log the fraction of items with a_i > 0 as a data check decided before training, not a tuned constant.
ideas.spec_equations:
graph: c_ij from window-5 session co-occurrence on train; w_ij = c_ij/(sqrt(pop_i pop_j)+1); pi_ij = w_ij / sum_k w_ik; m_i = sum_j w_ij; a_i = m_i/(m_i+median(m)).
  lift: x_i = exp^K_o( [0, e_i / ||e_i||] ) with e_i the frozen text embedding, tangent scale fixed at 1.
  anchor: b_i^(0) = exp^K_o( sum_j pi_ij log^K_o(x_j) ); repeat 3 times b_i^(t+1) = exp^K_{b_i^(t)}( sum_j pi_ij log^K_{b_i^(t)}(x_j) ).
  target: t_i = exp^K_{x_i}( a_i * log^K_{x_i}( b_i ) ), then clamp with t_i <- exp^K_o( min(1, R/||log^K_o(t_i)||) * log^K_o(t_i) ), R = 99th percentile of ||log^K_o(x_i)||.
  encode: u_i = log^K_o(t_i) (D-dim tangent vector); z = E(u_i) in the tangent space at o, mapped in as Z_i = exp^K_o(z).
  level 1: k_1 = argmin_k d_K(Z_i, c_1k); r_1 = log^K_{c_1 k_1}(Z_i).
  level l+1: v_l = log^K_o( exp^K_{c_l}( r_l ) ), p_l = exp^K_o( v_l ), k_{l+1} = argmin_k d_K(p_l, c_{l+1,k}), r_{l+1} = log^K_{c_{l+1}k}( p_l ).
  loss: sum_l [ d_K( sg(p_l), c_{l,k} )^2 + beta * d_K( p_l, sg(c_{l,k}) )^2 ] + || dec( log^K_o( exp^K_o( sum_l ... ) ) ) - e_i ||^2 with the baseline MSE in the Euclidean tangent, beta kept at the baseline default.
  steering: only the target t_i and the residual geometry change; the optimizer, schedule, batch size and epoch count are the frozen ones.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: frozen text embeddings e_i for 24556 items, the sparse co-consumption table (top 20 per item, pi and m), the curvature parameter theta, the L codebooks. Output: a per-item Lorentz target t_i (and its tangent vector u_i), a per-step curved RQ forward pass returning the level codes k_1..k_L, the transported residuals and the curved commitment/reconstruction loss; the emitted SID is the code tuple, unchanged in format from the baseline.

specification.text: See SPEC EQUATIONS. In one line: t_i = exp^K_{x_i}( a_i * log^K_{x_i}( b_i ) ), b_i = Frechet_K({x_j : j in N(i)}, pi_ij), a_i = m_i/(m_i + median(m)), and the RQ chain is r_1 = log^K_{c_1}(z), r_{l+1} taken as the log of p_l = exp^K_o(PT(r_l)) at the next code, all distances d_K.

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
